key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches virtual perovskite solar-cell shortlists for candidates near high-performing measured devices.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help prioritize device recipes for fabrication across large composition, layer, and processing search spaces.
method: Generate recipes with learned policies guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support using 890 measured reference devices.
Compare three policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices increased mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74% through top-ten selection; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates were 23% for PPO and 24% for recurrent PPO, versus 2.9% for Pure Random.
watch_item: Neighborhood enrichment does not establish fabricated-device performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget superiority; many generated recipes also have weak experimental support.
paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
